sources._: STUB — hand-authored 2026-08-20 from the files named below so the viewer runs before the build pipeline exists. Replace with configurator/build/out/positions.json.

frame.name: board
frame.definition: The case model's xy board frame. Origin at the PCB's (0,0) corner; x -> physical RIGHT, y -> physical FRONT (toward the user), z -> UP with z = 0 at the PCB top face. Millimetres.
frame.handedness_source: release/hardware/case/v2/agentpad13_case_v2.py — the design frame is LEFT-handed (x right, y DOWN from raw KiCad coords, z up) while STL/STEP are right-handed.
orientation_facts: USB (J1) is at y = 3.05, the FAR edge away from the user.
Encoder at x 13.525, stick at x 69.710; board +x is the owner's RIGHT.
Rendered as reality: encoder BACK-LEFT, stick BACK-RIGHT, 2U key at the FRONT.

to_gltf.note: Meshes in meshes/*.glb are ALREADY in glTF's Y-up right-handed space. To place a position from this file into that space use (X, Y, Z)_gltf = (x, z, y)_board. That swap has determinant -1, which is what converts these left-handed board-frame numbers into the correctly handed real device; the usual det +1 Z-up->Y-up rotation (x, z, -y) would render the MIRROR IMAGE.

mesh_placement.note: 'baked' meshes already carry their assembly position in their vertex data — load and add to the scene, no transform. 'instance' meshes sit at their own local origin and must be placed using the positions in this file.

instance.cap_*: place at (switch.x, keycap_seat_z, switch.y) in glTF space; cap local origin = centre of the bottom rim, +x along the 2U long axis
instance.knob_*: place at (encoder.x, 0, encoder.y); the knob mesh already carries its absolute z (skirt bottom .. knob top)
instance.stick_cap_*: place at (stick.x, 0, stick.y); the cap mesh already carries its absolute z (14.4 .. 19.6)
instance.switch_mx: site-owned stand-in; place at (switch.x, 0, switch.y), absolute z 0 .. 15.2 (stem top)
instance.screw_m3: site-owned stand-in; place at (screws.positions[i], 0), absolute z tip .. head_top

site_baked.stabilizer_2u: site-owned stand-in for the 2u plate-mount stabiliser; BAKED at the absolute stabilizer.slot_centers because its wire is not symmetric in y

stab._: STUB — the same stabiliser, in the block name the generated file uses.

screws._: STUB — the four M3x8 ISO 7380 button heads that hold the stack together (release/HOW-TO-ORDER.md step 6, hardware/case/agentpad13_case_v2.py §'One screw path'). Proud on the deck: seat at the plate top, head top 1.8 above it.

touch_pad._: STUB — TP5, the capacitive touch pad. The three plate variants differ ONLY in how it is finished, which is the whole visible difference between them.

bases._: STUB — the richer per-variant base block. The viewer only needs tilt_deg; hinge/desk_plane are here so the shape matches the generated file.
bases.note: A base's flat top IS the tray bottom (mating_plane_z), so a base mesh needs no transform — it is baked. What the viewer needs from here is the LEAN.
bases.tilt_axis: board x. A tilt raises the FAR edge (y = 0, the USB edge) and leaves the NEAR edge (y = 100, the 2U key edge) down on the desk.

pedestal._desk_z: A Ø78 disc centred at y = 50 spans y 11..89 and never reaches the y = 103.7 hinge line, so its desk face is a SLICE of the wedge plane: -11.9 - (103.7 - y) * 0.140541 at both ends.
